items.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
items.desc: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

items.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
items.desc: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

items.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships across country in midterm elections
items.desc: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor. She discusses the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children. “There was a realisation across the map that perhaps moms were the best messenger for this,” she explains, pointing to voters' concerns about “the cost of living, affordability, how to make ends meet.”

items.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
items.desc: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

items.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
items.desc: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

items.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
items.desc: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.

items.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
items.desc: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

items.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
items.desc: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

items.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
items.desc: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

items.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
items.desc: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

items.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
items.desc: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

items.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
items.desc: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.

items.title: French Ciryl Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit
items.desc: Ciryl Gane remains the world's MMA heavyweight champion. Overnight, the French athlete beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in ​New York. The 5-round fight was rough, as Shirli Sitbon explains.

items.title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
items.desc: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

items.title: France's presidential race heats up
items.desc: In approximately six months' time, French voters will head to the polls for the first round of the presidential election. Due to term limits, current president Emmanuel Macron is barred from running again. But that hasn't stopped a whole host of candidates from tossing their hat in the ring.

items.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's petrochemical capital in overnight assault
items.desc: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that the central industrial city of Nizhnekamsk had endured "prolonged" Ukrainian airstrikes overnight, damaging a residential building and sparking a fire at a major petrochemical complex, injuring three people. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.

items.title: The Philippines and Australia strengthen joint military deterrence at ASEAN summit
items.desc: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. During three days, world leaders are expected to focus on trade, energy and conflict – including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is expected to land in Manila on Tuesday. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.

items.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
items.desc: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian president also claims that Russia has rejected an energy truce. This week’s US-mediated negotiations did not result in any tangible progress. Story by Simon Moritz.

items.title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
items.desc: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.

items.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia, overshadowed by tensions in Africa
items.desc: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov.

items.title: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
items.desc: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.

items.title: Are we too reliant on technology? Questions arise after Microsoft's widespread outages
items.desc: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.

items.title: Pope laments poverty-stricken Inca communities as locals leave Peru
items.desc: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.

items.title: COP31：气候资金难满足需求，各方呼吁污染者“买单”
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）周五聚焦气候资金问题。联合国秘书长古特雷斯警告，即使将提供给脆弱国家的气候适应资金增至三倍，也只能满足其需求的不到三成。与会者呼吁富裕国家和主要污染者承担应有责任，为受气候灾害影响的国家和社区提供更多支持。

items.title: 联合国：海湾局势持续紧张对国际和平与安全构成严重风险
items.desc: 联合国负责政治事务的助理秘书长希阿里周五在安理会通报中东局势时表示，霍尔木兹海峡和曼德海峡及其周边地区局势持续紧张，对国际和平与安全、地区稳定和全球经济构成严重风险。他呼吁各方立即停止袭击民用船舶，恢复航行自由，通过外交途径寻求和平解决方案。

items.title: 联合国环境署：空气污染不仅是环境问题，更是健康与经济危机
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会举行之际，德里及印度北部多地再次被浓重雾霾笼罩。联合国环境规划署表示，空气污染已不仅是环境问题，更是一场影响公众健康和经济发展的危机。

items.title: 世卫组织在中国设立新的全球合作中心 推进性传播感染预防与创新
items.desc: 世界卫生组织周五宣布，正式指定位于中国广州的南方医科大学全球健康研究院为新的“世卫组织性传播感染预防与创新合作中心”。此举旨在加强全球预防和控制性传播感染的合作，重点推动创新、扩大检测可及性、加强监测以及提升公共卫生能力，特别是在中低收入国家。

items.title: 刚果（金）：武装袭击阻碍埃博拉疫情防控
